- **Decision for Shahzaib (S7-F10 security review) — the minimum-commission oracle:** an agency can learn whether a network listing pays at least N % by setting its CUSTOM site's minimum commission to N and seeing whether the listing stays on the site (it predates S7-F10: S7-F4's rule; the view only made it faster). Binary-searching N gives another agency's commission to the basis point in ~14 edits. If network agencies must not infer each other's commission: rate-limit edits of a site's minimum commission (e.g. a few per day per agency) and audit them (who, when, old → new), or allow only coarse steps (whole percent). Not built — say which, if any. **Answered 2026-10-25: limit and log → S12-F25.**

- **S5-03 design notes (done 2026-10-18 — as built, see the S5-03 row and Decisions):** a `search_index_queue` row (target, agency, queued_at) written in the same transaction as each read-model change (upserted or deleted targets) → zero lost updates while search is down; `search.syncIndex` (debounced after read-model jobs + every minute) claims ≤ 500 rows with a lease (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, one holder per row so pushes stay ordered), builds docs with `search.indexDocsFor`, upserts/deletes, waits for the engine task, then deletes only rows whose `queued_at` is unchanged; nightly drift check samples targets (sourceHash vs index) and index docs (exists in read models), enqueueing mismatches; a repair job walks everything when the sample finds drift.

| S1-F2 | DONE | 2026-10-12 | Outbox hardening (ADR 0014 implemented). **Poll only:** `emit()` and `replayOutboxBatch` send no NOTIFY; dispatcher lanes poll every 250 ms and claim again at once after any non-empty batch; `DATABASE_URL_LISTEN`, `@inmolink/db` `listen()` and the `app_listen` follow-up are gone (config, worker, `.env*.example`, Kamal, Ansible). **Per-tenant fair claim:** one SQL statement enumerates the agencies with due rows (recursive loose index scan, one probe each, ≤ `maxAgenciesPerClaim` = 64 agencies per claim, per-lane rotating cursor with wrap-around so every agency is reached within ⌈due agencies / 64⌉ claims), shares the batch by water-filling (small agencies take all they have, the rest split the remainder), takes each agency's oldest rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and interleaves them round-robin; the per-agency count probes stop at the equal share and then at the level the small agencies leave the others, so a claim reads about 2 × `batchSize` index entries for counting plus the rows it locks — O(batchSize + 64), not O(backlog) or O(agencies). Migration 0029 re-keys `outbox_events_pending_idx` to `(agency_id, available_at, id) where processed_at is null`; 0030 (custom) sets aggressive autovacuum/analyze thresholds on `outbox_events` (queue table: insert, two updates, delete). **One `PLATFORM_AGENCY_ID`:** new leaf `@inmolink/platform/tenancy`, re-exported by `platform/outbox`; `db/tenancy/rls.ts` and the registry predicates import it; a workspace test fails if the literal appears anywhere else. **Subscriber idempotency** is a PATTERNS §8 / workers.md rule (delivery tracked per event; a retry re-runs every subscriber) instead of per-subscriber tracking. Tests: `[S1-F2]` 50,000-event burst + 9 other agencies → every other agency's event is in the first batch of 500 (dispatcher with a 5,000-agency cap, so the dozens of agencies earlier suites leave in the shared table do not push ours out of the first rotation); 150 agencies × 3 rows with 64 per claim → three claims in rotation, each agency served by exactly one claim, no agency twice before all once; idle lane picks up an event in < 500 ms (250 ms poll + delivery); platform id defined once. **Perf (local, Windows + Docker Desktop):** outbox dispatch of 30 k events (30 agencies × 1,000), final build: per-10 k windows 1,522 / 2,850 / 3,666 ev/s, overall 2,342, measured right after a 170 k-row insert/delete churn on the table; the one-pass build an hour earlier on a quiet table: 3,798 / 3,370 / 3,885, overall 3,670 (S0-06 baseline: 1,806 / 3,075 / 3,085, overall 2,494); zero loss across a redis-queue restart. Claim plan (`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, all index scans, no Seq Scan): 50 k burst + 9 × 1 + 107 platform rows → 13 ms; 600 agencies × 200 rows → 74–124 ms, of which locking the 500 rows is ~65 ms on this disk (the pre-S1-F2 claim on the same data: 177–252 ms; the fair-share CTEs alone, no locks: 5–6 ms) |

Hero without `decoding=async`, `fetchpriority=high`; `sizes` capped so phones take the 640w variant; `preconnect` to the media CDN. **Gate** (`proxy.ts` → `server/embed.ts` `embedGate`): the client's per-IP page limit first (`embed.page` 60/min, 2,000/day — made-up ids cost one Redis call), then `embedSiteScope` (scope only, no inventory), then the **gate marker** — HMAC of the site id with `HMAC_KEY` in `x-inmolink-embed-gate`, replacing any client copy; every embed route refuses (404) without a valid marker and loads the site again (a tampered id is refused). Other spellings of an embed path (`/%65mbed/…`, `/EMBED/…`, `//embed/…`, upper-case ids) are a 404 at the proxy; the matcher includes every `/embed` path (dots too). Every other route: `X-Frame-Options: DENY` + `frame-ancestors 'none'` (proxy and `next.config`). Requests without a client address share one bucket, logged once a minute with the count (a bad `TRUST_PROXY` shows). `PUBLIC_URL` (https) is required in production like `TRUST_PROXY`. `experimental.inlineCss` removed again (the embeds are no Next pages; portal bundle unchanged). **Leads**: POST to the detail URL → contract `WebsiteLeadBody` (16 KB cap) → `checkEmbedLimits` (site × IP: the website forms' 5 / 10 min, 20 / day) → core `submitEmbedLead` = S7-05 `submitLead` as a browser form (Turnstile solved on the public pages host `PUBLIC_URL`; the presenting agency's lead). **Dashboard** (`/websites/[id]`): XML feed card — on/off, the token's last characters, last run, Kyero vs generic counts ("—" when unknown), last error; "Turn the feed on" / "New token" send a per-render `Idempotency-Key` (a repeated submit answers the same token, S7-07) and show both URLs once on `FEED_API_PUBLIC_URL`; "Turn the feed off"; IFRAME sites show their embed address on `PUBLIC_PAGES_URL`; EN + ES. Kamal: public secrets/env, web feed and pages hosts. **`pnpm perf:lighthouse`** (`scripts/perf/lighthouse.ts` + fixture with photos: WebP variants of the pipeline sizes in the test MinIO, set on the read models): `--url …` audits served pages; without, seeds an IFRAME site, starts the public production build and audits search + detail — mobile, simulated throttling, `--runs` 3, each number the median; fails below 90 (performance, accessibility, SEO; `--allow-noindex`) or at LCP ≥ 2,000 ms. **Numbers (local, median of 3 runs, mobile):** search — performance 100, accessibility 100, SEO 100 (noindex excused), best practices 100, FCP 726 ms, **LCP 1,271 ms**, TBT 34 ms; detail — 100 / 100 / 100 / 100, FCP 721 ms, **LCP 1,249 ms**, TBT 55 ms (runs 100 / 97 / 100). Before the rework: 80–94, LCP 2.2–2.5 s, TBT 230–740 ms. JS: no framework on embeds (route handlers); detail page 1.5 KB own script (0.7 KB gzip); portal routes unchanged (framework 131.7 KB, route 13.6 KB); dashboard `/websites/[id]` 176.6 KB first load. **Tests `[S7-F8]`:** core unit ×4 (`embed-branding.test.ts`), core int ×5 (`embed.int.test.ts`: embed identity incl. suspended / deleted / other mode / no domain, no server-side fetch; network detail white-labelled, ≤ 3 statements; a lead reaches the presenting agency through Turnstile on the pages host, fails closed without it; **unknown ids cached as missing**; per-IP limits), public unit ×14 (`proxy.test.ts`: gate marker set and a client copy replaced, refused / limited 404 / 429 with DENY, **encoded / upper-case / double-slash spellings refused**, other routes still DENY, every embed path matched; `csp.test.ts`: static CSP, next.config DENY on all paths but embeds, embed paths, the script self-contained and hashed; `views.test.ts`: texts escaped, unsafe URLs / colours dropped; `jsx-runtime.test.ts`: escaping, prop mapping, handlers refused; `env.test.ts`: **`PUBLIC_URL` required in production**), public int ×4 (`embed.int.test.ts` on the route handlers: **the rendered iFrame detail page and result cards pass the white-label check with no framework script**; static CSP + frame-ancestors + no X-Frame-Options + `s-maxage=60` + `Cache-Tag`; 404 without / with a forged / another site's marker and for a WordPress site; **a lead posted from the page reaches the presenting agency**, plain post → 303 with the notice, **a tampered site id is refused and stores nothing**), web unit ×1 (`feed-actions.test.ts`: **the form's Idempotency-Key reaches the API**), e2e ×1 (`website-feed.spec.ts`: an admin turns the feed on, copies the URLs, rotates and turns it off). The S7-02 white-label assertion moved to `core/src/testing/white-label.ts` (`whiteLabelLeaks`, exported from `@inmolink/core/test`); `db/test` prune also deletes `feed_sheet_releases`. **Checks run:** typecheck (public, web, core + earlier contracts / i18n / db, root), lint (+ root), boundaries (check + test), i18n:check, unit (public, web, core website-api / websites, contracts, i18n), int (core website-api + websites, feed-api website-api / leads / site-feeds, api websites, public), e2e website-feed, workspace deploy-config, perf:bundle, perf:lighthouse. **Security follow-up** (Decisions › Embed hardening): urlencoded-only bounded lead bodies (415 / 413, chunked included), `no-store` without purge tags and on `?lead=` pages, URL / event-handler / raw-HTML / style rules in the HTML runtime, time-bound gate marker, `<noscript>` notice; tests `security.test.ts` (chunked oversize cancelled at the cap, multipart / JSON / lying length refused, marker per minute, caching without tags), runtime ×3 more (handlers any case; `javascript:` / `data:` / `vbscript:` dropped in mixed case, with whitespace or control characters; raw HTML and styles), int (notice page `no-store`, multipart 415 at the route, a two-minute-old marker refused). | S7-F9 | BLOCKED-HUMAN H4 | 2026-10-22 | Index-driven fallback search for network sites (S7-08 perf audit, ⚡; no migration, no index, no dependency). **Cause** (EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the 500k-row fallback seed): not the candidate set — `m` stops at the count's cap through `price_idx` (≤ 1.3k rows) — but the **null phase** of a nullable sort: with a price band (`price_cents is not null and …`) the branch for rows without a price (`… and price_cents is null order by target_id`) is a contradiction the planner does not see, so it walked the whole table in id order for 25 rows that cannot exist (`listing_search_docs_pkey`, 502,273 rows removed, 184–253 ms here; a Seq Scan under the container's `random_page_cost` 4 — the audit's 13–1,055 ms and the 2 s timeout). **Fix** (`search/repo.ts`): `requiresValue(filter, sortField)` — an `and` holding a range / `eq` / `in` on the sort field, or an `or` whose every branch does — makes the null branch `where false` (a one-time filter, no scan; a forged phase-1 cursor on such a filter ends the results). Every other shape was already index-driven: `price_idx` / `beds_idx` / `area_idx` / `newest_idx` keyset walks with an early stop at `limit + 1`. **No composite index for the network branch**: the network rule matches ~85 % of rows, so the sort-index walk stops within a few hundred entries, and `listing_search_docs` is a hot write table (rewritten with every read-model refresh; 1.1 GB with its indexes at 500k rows) — `(share_scope, status, sort)` btrees would tax every write for nothing measured. **Estimable negations:** the network rule's `not ownerAgencyId = self` / `not networkHidden = true` compiled to `not coalesce(…, false)` (default selectivity: a network filter was estimated at ~1 % of its rows); now `owner_agency_id <> $1` / `<> all(…)` on never-null columns and `network_hidden is not true` / `is not false` (same meaning; nullable scalars, arrays and `ref` keep the general form) — the deep network sitemap page's estimate went 372 → 1,449 rows and, where the estimate allows, the plan from a bitmap over half the network + sort (56 ms) to the `public_code_idx` walk (3 ms). **`sitemapDeep` (S7-F7 note):** the 316–487 ms p95 was the test — its five deep pages were warmed three of five and evicted by the endpoints measured before them, so 5 of 50 reads (10 %) were cold pages (`sitemapColdPageMs` 377–463 ms, 128 MB shared buffers) and the p95 was a cold read; now warmed right before measuring (67 / 141 ms in two runs). What remains locally is test data: this run's country holds every `Z…` code but 19 % of the table (other suites' 500k rows), so the planner keeps a bitmap + sort for that page; where the country holds the network (staging, production) the estimate favours the code-index walk. **Degraded-engine k6 profile:** `degraded` (S7-08's 1,000 rps × 15 min and thresholds, refuses overrides) + metric `search_degraded` (searches answered `degraded: true`), a threshold > 99.9 % in degraded runs so an engine that still answers fails the run; `DEGRADED=1` override; `pnpm perf:smoke` passes it unless `--engine`; summary "search engine stopped … searches from the fallback n %"; runbook step 5b (stop → `SearchFallbackActive` → run → start → resolves). **Perf** (local, 500k rows, containers lifted to 4 CPU / 4 GB): `[S7-F9]` 21 shapes × pages 1–2: p95 7–43 ms, widest scan 1.2k–4.9k rows, slowest EXPLAIN 2–10 ms (one 80 ms warm-up outlier); EXPLAIN network + band + `price_asc` before 253 ms (pkey walk, 502k rows removed) → after 4.3 ms (`price_idx`, 1,278 rows read, null phase `One-Time Filter: false`); `[S5-04]` p95 52–54 ms overall. **`pnpm perf:smoke` (engine stopped, 20 rps, 60 s): exit 0** — 1,203 requests, errors 0 %, searches from the fallback 100 %, p50 / p95 / p99 20.8 / 47.5 / 90.6 ms (S7-08: p95 124 ms and one 2 s timeout), search p95 52.5, `changes_since` 37.4, 1.92 statements per request. - 2026-10-21 · **Minimum commission (S7-F4):** (1) **The fallback cannot read the commission:** it lives in `listing_search_commissions` (worker-written, no application grant) and `app_public` only gets a yes/no per target from the SECURITY DEFINER `search_commission_at_least` (security review M1; a column grant would not do: filtering needs SELECT). A compromised feed-api could still probe one target at a time by bisection; it can no longer list commissions. Cost: ~7 µs per candidate row (shape 13 median 28.8 ms, fastest 18.7 ms vs the 20 ms gate: thin). **If it breaks the budget at 2M rows the fallback is a whole-percent band** (`floor(bp / 100)` in a readable column, with the minimum restricted to whole percent) — not built. (2) **Index document only, read models unchanged** (S5-01 decision 4): read at build time; `write()` syncs the commission rows of every rebuilt target (two statements, only changed values written) so a commission-only edit is pushed. (3) **Fixed commissions:** share = floor(fixed × 10,000 / price) in the price's currency; another currency, an on-request or missing price is unknown and excluded when a minimum is set; VAT flag ignored. (4) **A minimum needs network listings** (contract refinement). (5) **Network sites need a verified agency** (M2: an unverified agency could probe commissions through its own CUSTOM site): refused on save and failed closed (own listings only) at serving time. The **give-to-get gate is still S7-03's job** (drop `networkOf` for a LOCKED agency where the website API builds the scope). (6) Existing documents have no commission until the repair walk / rebuild; a site with a minimum then shows no network listings (fail closed).

PATTERNS §19 unchanged. Option (B) (zero-JS HTML portal pages) stays on file in the ADR.

(3) "Non-migrated" = no billing history (subscription, customer, grant or price lock) when onboarding finishes; the legacy agency import (S14) or staff must set the founding grant/price lock **before** the agency onboards, or it also gets the trial (harmless: the higher plan wins). (4) The trial starts at first onboarding (sign-up's app_auth tx can only emit identity events). (5) Founding lock = a repeating Stripe coupon for the difference, months until the lock ends; free parallel run = a staff Pro grant until the old provider's renewal. (6) Dunning notice = `billing.dunning.started` + the billing page banner; Stripe's own retry emails meanwhile (admin email/in-app notice → S13-F22). (7) Only features that exist today are gated at their entry points; quotas (sites per plan, social accounts, 100 Free contacts, AI caps) and serving-side checks → S13-F21. (8) Staff grant/revoke/price-lock audit-log rows are written by S13-03's console routes (the grant row records who, why and until when; a lock change keeps only the latest values until then).

- 2026-10-23 · **S9 review fixes:** (1) **One budget for the `exports` pool's heavy jobs:** event passes, nightly passes, push runs and site feeds share a cap group (`EXPORTS_FEED_CAP_GROUP`, new `capGroup` in platform/queue) — at most `runsPerProcess` (2, the measured-safe number) per process and `maxConcurrentRuns` across the pool, whatever the mix; a nightly pass hands its slots back (`releaseCapSlots`) before it queues its lane's successor; boot requires `nightlyLanes` < `maxConcurrentRuns` (other heavy jobs always keep a slot); a nightly job can still find its process full and go back to delayed (at most the lanes' few jobs) — size the pool so processes × `runsPerProcess` ≥ `maxConcurrentRuns` (4 processes at the defaults). - 2026-10-23 · **Local windows only while failing open (S8-F9, after security audit):** (1) Counted always, enforced only on `failedOpen` — windows filled while Redis answered apply as soon as it fails. (3) The recently-valid map is keyed by edge token (SHA-256 of key + origin), ≤ 10,000 entries, oldest dropped. (4) The publishable per-key form cap is always enforced (no shared twin), peeked before the round trip. (5) Untracked form posts: a per-key budget (`u|keyId`, the key's hourly lead limit) plus a global 1,000 per hour (refusal scope `ip`: `RateScope` has no process scope); constants, not config. (6) The under-limit list is oldest first; a window back under its limit (release, raised tier) is appended.

- 2026-10-23 · **One in-process limiter (S8-F6, after code + security review):** (1) **No refuse-on-full anywhere:** the first cut refused new identities when a pool was full, which let 10,000 bad-key requests from distinct /64s (one IPv6 /48) make every new IP fail key-cache misses for every tenant, even with Redis healthy, and refused new browsers' posts. Now only a tracked window at its limit refuses; a full pool evicts its oldest window under its limit, never a boxed one, and leaves a new identity untracked when all are boxed (untracked = allowed; a browser's post still counts on its key). Trade-off: an attacker who boxes the whole map gets later addresses untracked locally (the shared rule still counts them while Redis answers). (2) **Window length per pool**, so the sweep is exact; the form-post windows are rebuilt (counts reset) when `leadWindowSeconds` changes. (3) **`key` pool rotation accepted:** someone holding more than 10,000 keys can rotate the `key` pool during an outage; each key still counts in the shared rules. (4) Eviction looks at most 64 windows from the oldest (bounded work per request when the front is boxed). (5) `LocalWriteCaps` / `LocalFailedChecks` removed rather than kept as wrappers; core imports `LocalFixedWindows` from `@inmolink/platform/rate-limit`. (6) Optional embed per-site cap not built. **Follow-up (logged, not yet in the backlog):** apply the local windows only while the shared limiter fails open (needs a degraded signal on the limiter's result), and a per-process cap on total failed key lookups during fail-open.

(2) **Canonical search URLs:** the form's parameter order is the canonical order; the form's submission (every field, empties included) and the page's links (no empties) are the two canonical shapes of one filter set — anything else (reordered, repeated, unknown, leading zeros, a dropped invalid amount) is private, so cache-busting variants never reach a shared cache, yet still served (no redirect round trip). (5) **Feed URLs with query parameters are private** (behaviour change; the table's `params: []`): the token URL is the only cache key; a private gzip client gets the signed-URL redirect as with the edge cache off. (7) **Review:** embed `stale-if-error` 300 s, not 86,400 — a page whose purge failed must not keep a removed domain's `frame-ancestors` for a day (the feed's reasoning); every edge decision checks the raw query's written form, so percent-encodings, `+`/blanks, repeats and a bare `?` are private (unbounded cache-busting otherwise); the rule is found from the matched route, never passed by a handler.

- 2026-10-22 · **Fallback status condition and the CI-only shape 13 plan (S7-F11 fix, CI runs 39755711349 / 39758344176):** (1) **Root cause:** a one-row index-only probe is priced with a whole heap page as soon as any page of the table is not all-visible (`ceil((1 − allvisfrac) × 1)`), so the commission probe costs 2.66 (primary key, same as `floor_idx`) instead of 1.56 unless `relallvisible = relpages` exactly. 6879363's VACUUM loop stopped at 99 %, CI's state (99.9 %) and production's normal one; at 2.66 a probe, PG 18's skip scan over `transaction_idx` (transaction type, status) for the 85 % status set won a BitmapAnd (a 425k-row bitmap, ~10 ms of CI's 19–22 ms). (2) **Fix, not a threshold:** a status set containing ACTIVE is compared as `(status = any(…)) is true` — a filter with the same statistics (leakproof under RLS), never an index condition; a set without ACTIVE (reserved units network-wide) stays indexable. (3) **The S7-F10 check no longer requires `floor_idx`:** it asserts an index probe per candidate (pkey or `floor_idx`, ~2 µs either way), no transaction-index bitmap, and runs settled and with one page not all-visible. `floor_idx` stays (index-only when settled); dropping it would be a contract step, not needed. Reproduced locally after `REINDEX TABLE listing_search_docs` (the test database's indexes are now CI-sized). **Fix:** when the filter has a location on its `and` spine, `m` (the capped match set) compares numeric ranges as `(…) is true` filters; the index-ordered branches keep them as index conditions (a band sorted by price walks `price_idx`), and without a location `m` is unchanged (S7-F9's network band shapes need the band's index). Trade-off accepted: a large region with a narrow band now filters the region's rows until `m`'s cap instead of ANDing a small band bitmap. No CI timing factor exists in the repo and none was added; the EXPLAIN check logs the costed plan of any shape over budget.

(2) **The resume decision is taken in the claiming transaction** (fenced): the fingerprint of what the run reads (connector, url, settings, credential ciphertext, mapping) must match — any edit of those starts the run over; re-saving the same credentials does too (new ciphertext; accepted, rare) — and the sink must confirm its seen references are intact (UNLOGGED table, S7-F3), else the run starts over rather than withdrawing blind. (4) **The run deadline's `FEED_TIMEOUT` is retryable** now that a retry resumes, and a retryable failure on a job's last attempt after progress becomes a new slice (each slice gets its own 3 attempts); `MAX_CLAIMS` 100 bounds a run that keeps failing (a 1,000-page account needs 20 slices). - 2026-10-22 · **Website extraction budgets and limits-Redis ops (S7-F7, after review):** (1) **Distinct counting with a HyperLogLog** (PFADD/PFCOUNT in the same script; `limits` ACL gains `+pfadd +pfcount`): bounded memory (≤ ~14.5 KB per identity and window, ~200 B for a visitor's few searches) and ~1 % error — the acceptance test allows ±2 % on the throttle point; rejected: one marker key per signature (≥ 130 B per distinct value). One HLL per scope, identity and window (flag and throttle share it); a value is recorded only for a request every enforced rule allowed — except the one new value that trips a rule already at its limit (an HLL cannot test membership without adding; the rule's penalty then stops further adds). Slicing windows are fixed clock hours: a slicer straddling the hour gets at most twice the budget before the flag. (2) **Slice signature from the parsed query** (review): the route's own Zod schema (strict), only filter fields plus the listings sort, canonical values — junk parameters cannot inflate a shared-NAT browser's count (the request is a 400 without a signature), a different sort is a new slice; `/v2/developments` (filter: `locations`) slices too, in its own namespace and the same HLL. (3) **Who is flagged:** per publishable browser (flag → honeytokens on deep pages + `no-store` on paged requests, then throttle); key-wide budgets **alert only for both key kinds** — a server-rendered site searches and opens details for all its visitors, so volume never flags a secret key (S7-04 rule kept). **Accepted (review):** per-browser rules are keyed by key × IP bucket, so a scraper rotating IPs evades the per-browser flags and throttles; the key-wide rules then only alert — `WebsiteScrapingDetected` fires for every `action`, `observed` included, and every alert goes to the ops e-mail receiver (the only paging route; critical ones repeat hourly), so it pages like the others. (4) **Change-feed credit (review must-fix):** only **secret** keys earn it — the WordPress plugin syncs with its secret key; a browser has no reason to read `/v2/changes` — and only **once per entry**: each UPSERT (`ref|changedAt`) goes into a per-key HLL kept 24 h after the last grant (`syncCreditSeenSeconds`), so re-reading a page, or the whole feed with an old `since`, earns nothing again; a listing that changes again is a new entry (one more legitimate fetch). Chosen over a stored change position because the feed's `(tx_id, seq)` position does not fit the limiter's counter-only ACL and windows of the feed may be re-read legitimately. Credits live an hour, capped at 20,000. `/v2/changes` pages now count under the paging rules (never flags a secret key's polling; a browser crawling it meets its limits). The credit call is **fire-and-forget** (one Redis call after the change page is built, failures counted by `inmolink.rate_limit.failures` and logged sampled), so every request keeps exactly one awaited Redis call; a plugin's very first detail may race its credit (harmless against an hourly budget). (5) **Suspicion only on paged requests** (S7-06 Decision 3 kept): a flag tripped on a first page or a detail is read on the browser's paged requests with a non-counting `peek` in the same call; first pages stay the key's shared, cacheable answer. Edge-cached first pages never reach the slicing counter (S7-06 accepted); distinct slices are mostly cache misses. (6) **Agency day:** keyed by the agency id (`feed.agency.quota`, 2M / UTC day, secret keys, counted last) so rotating (same key id) or adding keys starts no new budget; publishable traffic counts in `feed.agency.pk.day` (alert only) — browsers cannot lock out the agency's servers. (7) **Fail-open stays, but visible (review):** counter `inmolink.rate_limit.failures` → `RateLimitFailing` (critical, 5 min), and feed-api readiness `rateLimitScripts` runs both scripts as the `limits` user (`RateLimiter.selfTest`), so an ACL missing a command (NOPERM) or a full Redis (OOM) keeps a new release out of rotation; requests themselves still fail open (S7-04). (8) **Limits stay on redis-queue (memory math):** per active browser ≈ 760 B (S7-04) + ≤ ~540 B (S7-F7); at 1M browsers/day with a 200k-browser peak hour: S7-04 day keys 150 MB + minute keys ≈ 120 MB + S7-F7 ≤ 2 h × 200k × 540 B ≈ 220 MB; keys: 10,000 keys × 14.5 KB worst ≈ 145 MB (typical sparse ≈ 10 MB) plus credit HLLs for secret keys that sync (≤ ~14.5 KB each, typically < 1 KB); agency days ≈ 1.5 MB → **≈ 0.65–0.75 GB worst** vs production `maxmemory` 8 GB (db-1 has 64–128 GB) — under 10 %, BullMQ remains the main user; ~1,000 script calls/s at peak are cheap for one Redis thread. Move limits to their own noeviction Redis (only `REDIS_LIMITS_URL` changes) if counters stay above ~25 % of the ceiling or limit scripts take > 50 % of redis-queue's CPU. (9) **redis-queue `maxmemory`** per environment (`redis_queue_maxmemory`: staging 1 GB, production 8 GB): without a ceiling `redis_memory_max_bytes` is 0 and the S7-04 alerts can never fire. (10) **Exporter least privilege (review):** a keyless `exporter` ACL user on **both** Redis (INFO, SLOWLOG, LATENCY, CLIENT getname/setname/info, COMMAND INFO, CLUSTER INFO; no key, no CONFIG — CONFIG GET would show the default user's `requirepass`, no CLIENT KILL; redis-cache's from its own hex secret, never the cache password), `REDIS_EXPORTER_CONFIG_COMMAND=-` (`maxmemory` from INFO; verified locally), **`REDIS_EXPORTER_DISABLE_SCRAPE_ENDPOINT=true`** — redis_exporter v1.93's `/scrape?target=` logs in to *any* target with the configured credentials (README: one password across targets), a credential leak to whoever can reach the port (verified: 404 when disabled). Ports open to the monitoring host(s) only: ufw rules on the db host inserted above the WireGuard allow; the redis-cache exporter's Docker-published port in DOCKER-USER (`INMOLINK-METRICS`, ufw does not see published ports). `RedisExporterDown` (critical, 5 min) when a target or its Redis stops answering. Staging objects of a dead job are swept after lease + one download + 5 min; incomplete multipart uploads need the R2 lifecycle rule (no lifecycle-as-code exists in the repo: HUMAN-ACTIONS H3 and deploy runbook step 6). (2) **Caps:** 4 feed-image jobs per process (≈ 18 MB each at worst), 32 across the pool; the perf child calls `importFeedImages` directly, so the caps are not exercised there — it runs 5 at once, one more than a process takes. (3) **Prune loops instead of pg_partman**, each transaction bounded by runs (2,000) and cascading errors (≈ 10k, by `errors_logged`): 200k runs + 34k errors in 4.1 s locally, so even the 960k/day estimate fits the 10-min budget; partitioning `feed_runs` (PK change, cascade to `feed_item_errors`) is not worth it now — revisit if the prune's `more` warning shows up. (5) **`property_import_seen` UNLOGGED with a logged guard:** a crash or a failover empties the table under a run that may carry on (or leaves it empty on the promoted standby); the run's logged `items_seen` (incremented in each batch transaction with the rows `recordSeen` actually inserted) must equal the table's count before the anti-join, else `SeenRefsLostError` (classified INTERNAL, retryable; on the last attempt the run fails INTERNAL, still withdrawing nothing). The S7-F2 duplicate probe is blind after such a loss only until that check restarts the run. The table drops its agency FK with the unused index (rule: every FK indexed), like the staging table. **Accepted:** seen rows of a deleted agency stay until the 24 h prune; they hold `external_ref` only, no PII. (6) **`feed_image_queue_updated_idx` dropped** (0099): the sweep no longer reads it and every claim / release updates `updated_at`, so the index blocked HOT updates. - 2026-10-21 · **Import correctness and structure (S7-F2):** (1) **A duplicate ref: the first item wins**, the later ones are item errors `DUPLICATE_REF` (field `ref`), counted as failed — also when the first one failed (its ref is recorded as seen, so the listing keeps its state rather than taking a later copy). - 2026-10-21 · **CDN caching and purge (S7-06, after review):** (1) **Two independent isolation safeguards.** (a) `_k` in the URL: the origin answers `public` only to a request whose `_k` matches its key and `Origin` — a dropped rule or a zone-wide cache-everything rule still cannot share answers across keys, and token-less requests are never cacheable; the token is derived from the key the request already sends, so it proves nothing, it only splits URLs. (b) The Cache Rule's `vary` (every plan; header cache keys are Enterprise-only) passes `x-api-key` and `authorization` through and bypasses anything else. **`Origin` is not a vary passthrough header** (Workers `cf.vary` forbids it and Cache Rules may too): the browser origin lives in `_k` instead, public answers leave `Origin` out of `Vary`, private ones keep it (→ bypass). A key is one site with one inventory policy, so this is ADR 0012's "site scope" at key granularity; rejected: site hostnames (DNS + certificates per site), a signed site token (would serve key-less requests). Not a §3 change (ADR 0012 #5 note). (2) **Off by default**; the runbook orders rule → `--apply` read-back → flag → `--verify` per environment, production included. (3) **Quotas and scraping:** edge-answered requests reach no quota or paging rule — accepted: only first pages and details per key, and every cursor page and new query still reaches the origin. **A flagged caller's first page is not made `no-store`**: suspicion is evaluated on paged requests only (S7-04; peeking at penalty state on every first page would need a non-counting limiter call), and a first page never carries a honeytoken — it is the key's shared answer (tested). (4) **Purge by tag** (every plan); lists carry the tags of the listings they show — one tag per change, no fan-out over sites; a listing new to a list appears within 60 s. (5) **Purge source:** a new outbox event `search.publicDocs.changed` with the read models (purging on the listing event would let the edge re-cache the old document). (6) **Freshness bounds:** TTLs live in core, sitemap capped at 240 s, horizon = 2 × the longest TTL (fresh + one stale serve); real worst case without a purge 2 × TTL (10 min for a detail), plus 24 h stale while the origin is down (intended). Site and key purges are never dropped (they end access); a revoked key without a purge ends at the next revalidation (401, not cacheable — staging check). (7) **Budget:** per-agency coalescing in a redis-cache sorted set and a 5 s throttle per agency (≤ 12 purge requests/min per tenant); account-wide pacing through the job's `globalConcurrency` 1 Redis lease, held for the pacing interval by the adapter (no second limiter needed); default 250 ms fits Pro and up (plan not decided, H3), Free needs 12000. (8) **Agency events:** suspension and preferred-agency changes purge the affected sites' `s` tags; removing a preferred agency also rebuilds the owner's PREFERRED listings' read models (`search.readModel.preferredRemoved`), whose change purges their `t` tags. **Give-to-get lock changes have no event** (computed from share counts, `search.websiteNetworkOpen` cached): a site losing or regaining network listings follows within the list TTL (60 s) plus that cache — accepted. (9) **Tags are keyed hashes** (hex: Cloudflare compares case-insensitively). (10) **Taxonomy** stays public without `_k` (identical for every key and site) and goes private on unknown query parameters (its schema strips rather than refuses them); every website v2 query schema is `strictObject`. (11) The `stale-if-error` acceptance is modelled locally; the real check is the staging step.

(9) **The speed-to-lead test** emulates the dispatcher's poll for the test's own agency (a real dispatcher in the shared test DB would claim other test files' events; adding an agency filter to the production claim only for a test was not worth the risk); BullMQ, the jobs and the e-mail adapter are real — labelled "quiet stack, test dispatcher", the real path is measured in S7-08 / H4. (10) **After review — query budget ≤ 3:** no idempotency lookup up front; the row and its event are one writable-CTE statement (platform `emitFrom`), the replay lookup runs only when the insert did nothing, and a failed Turnstile check looks the key up once (so a double submit still answers the first lead). (12) **Branding on the envelope:** `fromName` (the site's presenting name) with the platform's own sending address (SPF/DKIM stay aligned) and `Reply-To` the site's contact. - 2026-10-21 · **Change-feed test flake (S7-03) and rebuild sweep chunks (S5-01):** (1) **Test bug, not product bug.** `/v2/changes` pages only rows of transactions below the reading snapshot's `xmin`, which is **cluster-wide** (xids are shared by every database), so a transaction open in another test file (seed, rebuild, `withAdminRollback`) holds the horizon and the feed rightly answers an empty page with the same cursor and `hasMore: false` — "poll again", nothing lost (the next page returned both rows once the horizon moved). `since` with nothing newer starts at the held horizon, so it may include earlier changes (documented at-least-once start). No per-file database or schema can isolate the horizon, so the tests commit a marker transaction and wait, bounded at 60 s (describe timeout 120 s), until `pg_snapshot_xmin` passes it (`settled()`; a timeout lists the transactions holding it); reproduced 2/2 failing under load with the search suites, then 3/3 + 3/3 green. (2) **Rebuild sweep:** `search.deleteBetween` takes an advisory lock per candidate target until commit, so it now deletes at most `sweepBatch` rows (≤ `READ_MODEL_SWEEP_MAX` 5,000, and `sweepBatch × concurrency ≤ MAX_LOCKS_IN_FLIGHT`) per statement and transaction, after the page's rebuild commits; a full chunk stops before its last target so each target is swept, counted and logged once.

(3) **Suspicion (honeytokens, `no-store`) only after a tripped rule:** a `/v2/listings` cursor chain at signed depth ≥ 50 (any key), or a publishable browser past 600 paged requests / 10 min (flag; 1,800 throttles). **Volume never flags a secret key** (a server-rendered site pages for all its visitors). (4) **Honeytokens** replace one card of a flagged caller's page at depth ≥ 10 with its own clone (no extra card to count, no near-duplicate; reference in the cloned card's style), are synthesized from the site's HMAC and stored nowhere; never in the sitemap (public sitemap.xml), change feed, developments, totals or facets; detail → 404 + alert. (5) **Redis memory:** about 760 bytes and 5 keys per browser (the day key ~150 B until UTC midnight, the rest 2–20 min) on noeviction redis-queue next to BullMQ — 1M distinct browsers a day ≈ 150 MB resident plus the minute-scale keys. Fixed-window keys expire at their reset. Alerts `RedisMemoryHigh` / `Critical` added; the exporter scrape job and **moving limits to their own Redis are an ops decision for S7-F7**, not this task. (6) **Client IPs:** feed-api trusts `X-Forwarded-For` only from Cloudflare ranges and the kamal network (`TRUST_PROXY`, infra/kamal/feed-api.yml), and the origin lock (`roles/docker` `inmolink-origin-lock`, DOCKER-USER chain) lets only Cloudflare reach 80/443 — a client cannot spoof its IP bucket. (7) Search cursors carry a signed, site-bound depth; cursors from before S7-04 (or after an `HMAC_KEY` rotation) answer 422 once. (8) **Deferred to S7-F7:** filter-slicing, detail / sync counting, a per-agency daily quota across keys. (9) **S7-01 Decision 6 closed:** `created_by` not granted to `app_public`; guard trigger on `website_sites`; no tenant DELETE.

- 2026-10-21 · **White-labelled free-text search (S7-F5):** (1) **Every document's indexed text is sanitized** (backlog choice), not separate network-only fields: one set of fields, the owner's identity is the same for every site, and the index stays the same size. (2) **Places are not sanitized:** they are taxonomy names, never owner text. (3) **Only the deterministic pass is indexed.** The S12-03 model pass stays serving-time only (cost, determinism). Identity terms it misses (names under 3 characters, misspellings, names split by other words) can still match. (4) **Names are folded and joined loosely** (accents, case, `[\s\u00a0\-_.'’]*` between words, possessive, the website's main label as a name): a listing that names a place spelt like the owner's full name loses those words — rare, and the whole name must match. (5) **Team members:** e-mails always; names only with two or more words (a single first name — "Ana" — is too common a word to remove). `agency_members` has no phone (users' phones are not stored). Members joining or leaving re-push nothing at once: the drift check catches the changed `sourceHash`. (6) **No name history:** an agency's earlier names are not stored anywhere, so they are not removed (a verified agency cannot rename without re-verification). (7) **Reindex is a deploy step:** every `sourceHash` changes; run the repair walk, with `SEARCH_NETWORK_FREE_TEXT=false` on feed-api until it has finished, then `true` (default). `ops:rebuild-read-models` does not re-push unchanged documents. (8) **Identity changes re-push the whole agency**, only when an identity field changed (event flag `identityChanged`; events from before it push). (9) **Fallback rows keep their pre-S7-F5 hash** (built without text): an identity change never rewrites them.

- 2026-10-20 · **Fair scheduler, anomaly guard, import health (S6-08):** (1) **Freshness via feed (user-approved 2026-10-19):** a listing present in a successful feed run counts as a freshness confirmation for the S3-08 out-of-date check — the same write as the confirm button (prompt and network hide cleared) — but only while the feed shows signs of life: some item added, changed or removed within `IMPORT_FEED_FRESHNESS_DAYS` (default 120, config). "Changed" is judged per item (import hash: values and resolved taxonomy), "removed" as an item that was in the previous run and is not in this one; a feed whose items are unchanged for longer than 120 days (even if its bytes differ, e.g. an export timestamp) stops confirming, so an abandoned export cannot keep listings "fresh". Confirmations are written at most once per 7 days per listing, after the run's commit. Existing connections got `content_changed_at` from their kept runs (migration 0084: runs that created, updated or withdrew). Answers S6-02 decision (11). (2) **Guard thresholds:** spike = items read > 5 × the median of the last 5 successful runs (needs ≥ 3 runs and a median ≥ 20); drop = > 30 % of the live listings that were in the previous run missing at once (needs ≥ 10), listings created in the same run excluded from the base. Factor and ratio are env config; the minimums are constants (`ANOMALY`). A run with no valid item is not judged (S6-02 already withdraws nothing then). (3) **A paused run ends FAILED** with `FEED_PAUSED_*` (no new run state): the run's earlier batches stay written (a spike stops before the crossing batch; with 500-item batches at most ~5 × typical items are written before the stop), nothing is withdrawn and no miss is counted. (4) **Resume:** agency admins and staff (SUPER_ADMIN, STAFF_DATA_OPS) — "accept the change" skips the guard for exactly the next run; without it the next run is judged again. A resumed scheduled connection is due at once. (5) **Agency notice** = the persistent notice on the feed pages plus the outbox event `imports.connection.paused`; in-app/email delivery waits for S11-04 notifications (no consumer yet). Alerts are Prometheus rules (`ImportFeedPaused`, `ImportQueueWaitHigh` > 15 min for 5 min). (6) **Global cap per job definition, not per queue:** `globalConcurrency` leases in Redis (BullMQ's `setGlobalConcurrency` would also cap feed images and bulk actions in the `imports` pool); over-cap jobs re-delay with backoff (≤ 5 s + jitter) — about 100 Redis calls/s with ~500 runs waiting, accepted; a scheduler-side cap is the way out if it shows. Default 24 (the simulation at 16 under the steady load came close to the 15-min budget). (7) **The 500-feed load test is a model** of the scheduling rules with synthetic durations (as asked: no real imports); the real queue's cap is tested in `tests/queue/fairness.int.test.ts`. (8) **Staff column grants** (security review): the RLS generator gained `staff.selectColumns/updateColumns` (column allowlists, guard-checked); staff never read a connection's URL, credentials or settings. (9) Staff resume has no `version` check (concurrent resumes are idempotent under the row lock; last "accept" wins).

- 2026-10-18 · **Search indexer (S5-03):** (1) **The queue is the durability, not job retries:** read-model writes queue index pushes in their own transaction (`search_index_queue`), so a search outage of any length loses nothing — sync jobs may fail and be dead-lettered; the every-minute sync drains the queue when the engine is back. Global table without `agency_id` (one push batches every agency; a single global drain has no per-tenant fair share — a 10k-listing import delays others by ~20 batches of 500, i.e. seconds). (2) **Single writer:** only `syncIndex` writes the index; drift check and repair only queue. Ordering rests on one holder per row (lease + claim token) and pushing the *current* read model, never an event's data. (3) **Rejected vs failing:** only Meilisearch document errors (`invalid_document_*`, `missing_document_id`, `max_fields_limit_exceeded`, `payload_too_large`/413) back a document off; timeouts, unreachable, 5xx and engine faults release the whole batch untouched. Rejected rows are logged at error level with their attempts — an alert on them belongs with S5 observability. (4) **Acceptance "stopped for 10 minutes"** is tested as an outage lasting until every sync job attempt is exhausted (~20 s), not ten wall-clock minutes: nothing in the queue expires with time (leases are released on failure), so the length does not change the path. (5) **Nightly cost at scale:** `count(distinct target_id)` over read models is ~3 µs/row (≈ 18 s at 2M targets × 3 locales) — fine for a daily worker job; if it nears the timeout, keep a per-target counter or count one row per target. Repair's index walk pages Meilisearch by offset (writes during the walk can skip a document; the next night finds it). (6) **Test seam:** `configureSearchIndex({ uid, scope })` (like `configureMedia`) points the indexer at a test index and limits it to one file's targets, because test files share one database and its queue; production never calls it. Security review suggested gating it on `NODE_ENV=test` — proposed for S5-F1, not done here. (7) **Freshness budget:** edit → searchable is `READ_MODEL_DEBOUNCE_MS` (2 s) + `INDEX_SYNC_THROTTLE_MS` (0.5 s) + the dispatcher poll (0.25 s) + engine time; p95 3.0 s locally.

- 2026-10-15 · **Media processing (S3-04):** (1) The original is deleted once processed: the normalized master (private, WebP q90, ≤ 2560 px) is the stored source of truth, variants are regenerated from it (PLAN §3 #33 "normalized master"); this also closes S1-F7's "stored without EXIF" check for listing media. The agency logo stub still stores its upload as is — re-encode it when the media manager UI (S3-06) touches logos. (2) Variant keys use an HMAC of the hash with a dedicated `MEDIA_URL_KEY` instead of the raw hash (S3-03 decision 3) — `v{pipeline}/{publicId}/{size}` rather than the backlog's literal `v{pipeline}/{sha}/{size}`. (3) "Byte-identical" holds for the same pipeline version and encoder stack: libvips picks SIMD code per CPU, so workers on different CPU types may encode slightly different bytes for the same key (visually identical); a unit test pins sharp/libvips/libwebp so an upgrade forces a pipeline bump. (4) WebP effort 2 (not the default 4): half the CPU for ~15 % larger files; needed for the 1.5 s budget on noisy photos. (5) Orphan cleanup deletes files before the record (S3-03 decision 2 said record first): the due record keeps every check asking for a fresh upload while files go, a failed delete is retried instead of leaking files nothing can find, and a re-use during the window resets the object to unprocessed for the reconciler. Accepted narrow race: an object re-used between its file deletion and record deletion can briefly lack its variants until reprocessed. (6) Processing failures for good: unreferenced → record dropped; referenced → `failed_at`, original deleted (EXIF), check answers UPLOAD; a fresh upload processes it again (job ID carries the event ID). (7) `requestVariants` is a system API without `ctx` (worker/read models); a route exposing it must authorize and rate-limit. (8) Security review findings deferred to S3-F4: media container still receives every worker secret (needs pool-aware config) and runs as `app_system`; public access to the media bucket must be limited to `v<n>/…` keys at the edge. (9) Throughput: ~0.9 s per 12 MP image per media process; the S3 exit criterion (10k listings with photos in < 1 h on staging) needs about (images ÷ 4,000) media processes — size the staging role accordingly (dedupe skips repeated photos).
- 2026-10-15 · **Media upload (S3-03), for S3-04 and later tasks:** (1) `media_objects` is global and keyed by the content hash (PK `sha256`, not a uuid: the hash is the identity); tenants only read it, the worker writes it (`withSystem`), so the RLS model is unchanged. `refcount` is eventually consistent (recount per event). (2) **S3-04's orphan cleanup must** lock the row (`for update`), recount `property_media` by hash itself (never trust `refcount`/`delete_after` alone), delete the row and only then the storage object; and sweep `originals/` objects ≥ 24 h old with no `media_objects` row (uploaded but never registered, or their sync event dead-lettered) — signed URLs make that unbounded until then (accepted; a per-tenant byte quota on `check` if abuse shows). A cascade delete of listings (hard purge, agency deletion) emits no event: purge jobs must emit `media.object.referencesChanged`, or the cleanup reconciles every object. (3) **S3-04 must** re-hash each original before processing (the signed checksum is enforced by MinIO; R2 to be confirmed — Handover) and never serve originals (EXIF): browsers get variants only. Public variant keys should not expose the raw SHA-256 (it links white-labelled sites to the owner's photos and lets a hash holder attach the object): derive them from an HMAC of the hash. (4) Accepted: any member who may list can learn whether a hash is stored anywhere (the dedupe the task asks for) and read its size/refcount; documents (VIDEO/DOCUMENT kinds) must not join this global namespace — a per-agency prefix and STRICT table when their task comes. (5) `mif1`/`msf1` HEIF brands are labelled `image/heic`; the decoder (S3-04) decides, in the sandboxed media worker. (6) `property_media.media_object_id` was dropped in the same release (no data existed), against expand → contract. (7) Clients set `content-length` themselves (browsers must); the other signed headers are sent as given; 412 on PUT = stored already, go on to register. (8) The "an uploaded JPEG is stored without EXIF" check (S1-F7) and the logo stub's re-encoding move to S3-04 (sharp arrives there).

- 2026-10-15 · **Staff list indexes under RLS (S2-F1):** no `(status, created_at, id)` index on `agencies`: under `app_staff` RLS the enum `=` is not leakproof, so Postgres never uses a status condition as an index condition (it stays above the policy filter). The keyset expression index gives the order and the status filters it; at ≤ 5,000 agencies a rare status scans the table in a few ms. Same rule for any RLS-read list: only leakproof conditions (uuid/text/int `=`, `<`) reach an index. Follow-ups (perf-auditor, not needed yet): the cross-tenant verification queue `agency_verification_requests_queue_idx` and per-agency lists (`agency_members`, `agency_invites`, `api_keys`, `preferred_agencies`) still sort; switch their time column to the keyset expression when they grow. The 24 months and when an archived month may be dropped are a legal question — confirm with the user before the first export (~2028-06). pg_partman skips a whole partition set on any error (e.g. a partition not owned by `app_owner`), new months included, with only a WARNING: add an alert on "fewer than 3 future audit partitions" with the monitoring work.

The batched script spans many keys, so redis-queue must stay a single node (or share a hash-tag prefix).

- 2026-10-12 · **S1-F3 platform and core cleanups.**
  - The BEGIN round trip carries the settings by intercepting the pooled client's first `query` call for the transaction (Drizzle offers no hook before `begin`; `SET LOCAL` needs literals just the same). Values are escaped with node-pg's `escapeLiteral`; the UUID values are regex-checked before, the reasons come from code. A multi-statement simple query cannot carry bind parameters, which is why literals are used at all. Drizzle sees the combined statement as `begin`, so `countQueries` excludes it as transaction control.
  - `countQueries` is a Drizzle logger hook, not a pg wrapper: `withSystemClient` (COPY streams) is not counted, and overlapping counts see each other's statements — count one scenario at a time. Budgets are written in statements (begin/commit excluded) unless a test asks for round trips.
  - The flag reload reads as `app_user` through `withGlobalRead` (read-only, no tenant), not `app_system`: the dashboard and workers have that URL, and `feature_flags` is a global table `app_user` may read. Without a reader (unit tests, scripts) the reload falls back to the caller's transaction as before.
  - Over-cap retry backoff is per process (an in-memory map by job id, cleared when the job runs, dead-letters or releases its slot); a job that moves to another worker starts again at the first delay — bounded, and no Redis round trip per retry.
  - Review and audit outcomes (S1-F3): the BEGIN hook is an own property deleted after the transaction (a stored `.bind()` grew per transaction); the transaction fails before any statement if BEGIN was not intercepted (audit settings must never be silently absent); the pooled client is destroyed only when a control statement (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK) failed, never for an error thrown by `fn`; `withSystem`/`withStaff` refuse NUL in reasons; pools pin `client_encoding: 'UTF8'` (the only encoding under which `escapeLiteral` is byte-safe); flag reads serve an expired snapshot while the reload runs or fails (stale-while-revalidate), so a saturated `app_user` pool cannot stall requests at the 60-second expiry; the generated policy test asserts every `CLIENT_MODE_ALLOWED` entry is a read action.
- 2026-10-12 · **S1-F2 outbox hardening.**
  - A lane claims again without a pause after *any* non-empty batch, not only a full one (ADR 0014 says "while batches are full"): a fair batch is cut by rounding and a trickle of small agencies can leave it under-full while rows are still due. An idle lane still costs one index probe per 250 ms.
  - The fair claim serves at most `maxAgenciesPerClaim` = 64 agencies per claim (each costs an enumeration probe, a count probe and a locking scan: 600 agencies with backlog measured 157 ms per claim uncapped, far over the 20 ms SQL budget) and rotates a per-lane cursor across claims, so every due agency is reached within ⌈agencies / 64⌉ claims — with 5,000 agencies all importing at once, under 80 claims, i.e. a few seconds, instead of one batch. Lanes keep independent cursors; `SKIP LOCKED` keeps them off each other's rows.
  - `outbox_events_pending_idx` now leads with `agency_id`. There is no longer an index ordered by `available_at` alone: nothing reads the oldest pending row globally (replay is by `id`; a future "oldest pending event age" metric would group by agency or add its own index).
  - Autovacuum settings for `outbox_events` are a custom migration (0030: vacuum at 1 % / 5,000 dead rows, insert-vacuum at 5 % / 10,000, analyze at 2 % / 5,000, cost delay 1 ms). No `fillfactor`: the claim and the acknowledgement both change indexed columns, so updates are not HOT anyway.
  - Delivery stays tracked per event (one `processed_at`), and PATTERNS §8 / workers.md now require each subscriber to be idempotent on its own, instead of a per-subscriber delivery table. Subscribers already enqueue jobs with stable IDs; the extra table would add a write per subscriber per event on the hottest path for a guarantee consumers must not rely on anyway (at-least-once).
  - Code review (S1-F2): the first cut counted due rows per agency up to `batchSize` — O(agencies × min(backlog, 500)), measured 221–339 ms (1.5 s cold) for 600 agencies × 200 rows. The probe now stops at the equal share `ceil(batchSize / agencies)`; agencies at the share are recounted up to the level the small ones leave them (a one-pass cap under-filled a 50 k burst + 107 platform rows + 46 small agencies to 356 of 500); the water level comes from the first agency at or above its probe limit. A big agency with fewer rows than a level raised twice can still leave slots empty in that batch; the lane claims again at once.
  - Security audit (S1-F2): the pg_hba rules and the ufw rule that let app hosts and the `kamal` network reach Postgres 5432 directly as `app_system` existed only for LISTEN; both are removed, so a compromised app host can reach the database only through PgBouncer (`127.0.0.1`). Migration 0029 rebuilds the pending index non-concurrently (fine before launch; a live system would need a `CONCURRENTLY` out-of-transaction migration).
  - `pnpm verify` (9 min, 58 tasks) had one failure on this machine: `tests/isolation/guard.int.test.ts` lost its `applyRls` lock-timeout race (`set local lock_timeout = '5s'`, "canceling statement due to lock timeout") while the queue and perf suites were hammering `outbox_events` in parallel. `pnpm test:isolation` alone passes (342 tests). Watch for a repeat; if it recurs, make `test:isolation` depend on `test:int:root` / `test:perf:root` in turbo.json so the ALTER TABLE statements never compete with the outbox load.
  - Two `pnpm verify` runs on this machine ended on unrelated Windows flakes: a Vitest fork worker of `@inmolink/app-api` `test:int` died with 0xC0000409 (the crash the vitest config already works around for the root projects with `pool: 'threads'`) and, once, the isolation guard's `applyRls` lock timeout above. Each suite passes when re-run alone. Tried `pool: 'threads'` in the shared Vitest preset: the core int suite's main process then died with 0xC0000409 twice under `verify` (a native-module crash in a worker thread takes the whole run down; forks are isolated), so forks stay and `pnpm verify` caps Turbo at `--concurrency=4` instead; `test:isolation` now depends on every package's int suite so `applyRls` never competes with them.
  - The throughput perf test keeps its `[S0-06]` tag and its ≥ 2,000 events/s check (ADR 0014 keeps it); the `restartRedisQueue` helper's `docker compose up --force-recreate` can fail on Docker Desktop for Windows (the container stays `Created`): start `redis-queue-test` by hand and re-run.

Modules that add a dashboard section register it there (PATTERNS: a module without tables is fine; it has no repo or schema).

- 2026-10-14 · **S1-F6 database and Redis operations.**
  - **Rate limits on redis-queue, not a third Redis:** the task offered redis-queue with a prefix or a `volatile-lru` split; `volatile-lru` would still evict counters (they carry TTLs), so redis-queue it is. Production connects as an ACL user confined to `inl:rl:*`; the test runs the real limiter as that user.
  - **Residual risks (security review), accepted for now:** (1) redis-queue has no `maxmemory`: a flood of distinct identities creates counter keys (each lives ≤ 2 windows) in the Redis that also holds jobs — add memory and `inl:rl:*` key-count alerts with the monitoring dashboards; a `maxmemory` cap would fail BullMQ writes too. (2) All apps share the `inl:rl:*` prefix, so a compromised feed-api could reset web's login counters; per-app prefixes and users if that matters. (3) api still holds the full `REDIS_QUEUE_URL` (it enqueues); a producer ACL user is a later hardening. (4) The limiter now shares a single-threaded Redis with BullMQ: a latency spike over 200 ms fails closed on `auth.*` rules — watch the limiter's fail-closed warnings.
  - **max_db_connections is per database, shared by every role:** long app_system work can still starve request roles, which now get a fast error instead of a 120 s hang. Per-role pool sizes when Stage B splits workers out.
  - **Users-phase budget:** the perf test asserts 15.2 s / 5 = 3.04 s, the review's figure; on this machine the old code took 6.1 s, so the same-machine speed-up is 3.2–4.7×. The 15.2 s figure came from an earlier, slower environment.

Acceptance check "an uploaded JPEG is stored without EXIF" is open and belongs to S3-03; verification images stay attachment-only downloads for staff until then.
  - **Dedupe, not `Idempotency-Key`:** the task allowed either; `(agency_id, sha256)` among unsubmitted documents needs no client change and no key store.

- **S9-02 assumptions:** (1) Portal exports read the agency's own `listing_read_models` (client-safe documents), not raw tables (CLAUDE.md rule 9); locales = the agency's content locales, base `en` else the first; a language's text is exported only where the listing has its own text in it. (2) thinkSPAIN and A Place in the Sun use the Kyero v3 format until H6 (the format common to Spanish portals; their own specs are unpublished); thresholds in `PORTAL_PROFILES` are assumptions (thinkSPAIN 3 photos / 50-char description, A Place in the Sun 5 / 100, Kyero 1 / 30, all max 50 photos / 20,000 characters, CEE required except generic XML) and are marked `confirmed: false` where unconfirmed. (3) CEE is also enforced when a listing is published (`ENERGY_RATING_REQUIRED`); the feed check is the second line (stale read model, exempt/pending cases). (4) Too many photos are cut at the portal's cap, never a reason to exclude; descriptions are never truncated (too long: excluded with the numbers). (5) The Kyero shape needs a priced listing: a price on request is excluded (`PRICE_ON_REQUEST`), as are nightly rents (`PRICE_PERIOD`). (6) Issue rows are written inside each batch's transaction before the sink runs, so a failed run leaves the latest checks; stale rows are removed only when a run completes. (7) `feed-xml.ts` moved to `core/src/feed-xml.ts` so `exports` does not import `website-api` (module boundary); its unit test stayed in `website-api/__tests__`. (8) Contract change: `PortalConnectionDto.validation` (nullable) and `PORTAL_ISSUE_CODES`; dashboard API only, no website-API SDK regeneration.

- **S9-02 review follow-ups:** (1) Runs of one connection must not overlap: S9-03 serializes them per connection (range deletes and summaries would interleave). (2) Perf note for S9-03: the batch reads (selection, documents) are per connection; an agency with several connections to different portals re-reads the same documents - run the connections of one agency in one pass (read each batch once, write to every sink) or keep batches large. (3) Contradiction to settle at H6/H14: the S6-07 *import* connector assumes a native `<thinkspain><property>` element format (names ASSUMED, H14), while the S9-02 *export* sends thinkSPAIN the Kyero v3 format (also unconfirmed, H6); the two assumptions are independent and neither is proof of the other. When thinkSPAIN's real specification or sample arrives, settle both from it (`imports/thinkspain/mapping.ts` and `PORTAL_PROFILES.thinkspain`). (4) `generated` is optional in `inmolink-feed-v1.xsd` (portal feeds omit it for deterministic bytes; per-site feeds still write it).

- **S9-03 assumptions (after the code, security and perf reviews):** (1) **Content hash = stream to a temporary multipart upload, then abort.** Each connection's XML is hashed (SHA-256 of the text) while it streams through gzip into `storage().upload` (5 MiB parts). An equal hash aborts the upload (UNCHANGED, no object); a different one completes it (WRITTEN). Hashing first would read and build every changed feed twice, and buffering would hold whole files. A feed under one part (nearly all) never leaves the process. The hash is of the XML, so a zlib upgrade cannot force a rewrite; it is also the strong ETag. `platform/storage` `abort()` now throws `StorageError` when the store refuses (404 = already gone). The feeds bucket gets an *abort incomplete multipart uploads after 1 day* lifecycle rule (runbook deploy.md step 6, H3).
  (2) **Serialization** is the agency's group lease: both pass jobs, `exports.generatePortalFeeds` (events) and `exports.generateNightlyPortalFeeds`, use group = agency with `concurrencyPerGroup` 1 in pool `exports`, and the lease key is per pool and group, so they never overlap for one agency. A WRITTEN run is recorded only if the served file is still the one the pass started from (compare-and-set inside one UPDATE). A run that loses is stored as FAILED `SUPERSEDED` with no size or hash, its object is deleted, and the nightly mark and validation totals still apply. No Postgres advisory lock: a pass spans many short transactions, and session locks do not survive PgBouncer transaction pooling.
  (3) **Nightly fairness = lanes** (review must-fix 2). The night is `EXPORTS_NIGHTLY_LANES` (6) chains, not 5,000 queued jobs. Agencies split into lanes by `hashtext(agency_id)`; each nightly job, when done (or failed for good), enqueues the next agency of its lane still due (one indexed statement, stable job id per agency and night). The 15-minute sweep only seeds or repairs the lanes (one statement: the first due agency per lane). With at most `lanes` nightly jobs at once (+ a successor queued as its predecessor finishes), nothing is picked up only to bounce off a cap. Site feeds and event passes find free slots all night: the real-queue test shows a site feed job starting within 3 s, never more than 2 × lanes nightly jobs queued, none ever in delayed. Nightly jobs have no pool-wide cap (the lanes are the cap; lanes ≤ `maxConcurrentRuns` is checked at boot) and at most `runsPerProcess` + 1 per process. Rejected alternatives: a sweep that tops up to the cap reacts only every 15 minutes (8 agencies per tick would not cover 5,000 in a night); a dedicated queue cannot share the agency's group lease with the event passes and site feeds (lease keys are per pool), so one connection's runs could overlap.
  (4) **Token lookup**: a SECURITY DEFINER `portal_feed_by_token(hash)` (owner `app_owner`, `definerRead` on `agency_portal_connections`) returns only what feed-api uses: connection id, channel, served run and content hash. It returns nothing unless the connection is enabled, its token unrevoked and its agency VERIFIED. `app_public` has no grant on the table, so a column added later cannot leak. There is no second constant-time compare: the row is found by equality on the unique keyed hash.
  (5) **What ends serving**: gone, off or revoked (not forced); the portal's writer turned off, no profile, or the agency not verified (forced, review should-fix 5). The next run deletes `portal-feeds/<connection>/` and forgets the served file, so a frozen feed is never served on; the nightly run guarantees this within a day. A suspension also purges every connection's `p` edge tag at once (`agencies.status.changed`), and the token lookup refuses an unverified agency immediately.
  (6) **Triggers**: listing changes (`search.publicDocs.changed`, `properties.listing.updated` with `tags`) queue one pass per agency, 5 minutes after the first. They are skipped while an import of the agency is QUEUED or RUNNING (`imports.agencyImportActive`, the small partial index `feed_runs_active_idx`); `imports.run.finished` then queues the pass. "Has a live connection" is cached per process for 60 s; a connection change drops the entry. A connection's own change runs within 1 minute, or 5 s for a new connection or token, and purges its URL at once.
  (7) **Nightly redundancy**: a full pass (every live connection, any trigger) that leaves nothing to retry sets `nightly_at`, so a listing-change pass after the window opened is tonight's run. Skipping agencies whose read models did not change since `feed_generated_at` was not done: withdrawals and purges remove read-model rows without leaving a newer `updated_at`, so `max(updated_at)` would keep a withdrawn listing in the feed until the next change.
  (8) **History**: `portal_feed_runs`, newest `FEED_RUNS_KEPT` = 30 per connection. Run ids (UUIDv7) are allocated when the pass starts, so history sorts by start. A pass records all its runs in 3 statements (the connections UPDATE via `jsonb_to_recordset`, one INSERT, one retention DELETE over the pass's connections). A failure to record the failed runs of a failed pass is logged (`err.name`), not swallowed. Reasons are the contract enum `PortalFeedRunReason` (DTO, core, web).
  (9) **Rate limits**: portals crawl many agencies' feeds from a few addresses, and a nightly regeneration purges them all. feed-api's per-IP limit for portal feeds is `PORTAL_FEED_IP_PER_MINUTE` (default 3,000/min, ≥ 60); the per-token limit (60/h) protects each feed.
  (10) **Memory**: one 5 MiB part buffer per connection in a pass, at most `runsPerProcess` + 1 passes per process. A 20,000-listing agency peaked at 384–404 MB RSS (budget 512); an agency with 20 connections and 20,000 listings is the outlier to watch on staging (H4).
  (11) `configureExports` takes an optional keyring: feed-api verifies tokens with `HMAC_KEY` and holds no encryption key. In production feed-api refuses to boot without `S3_BUCKET_FEEDS` (`assertFeedApiFeedsBucket`). Signed redirect URLs of portal feeds live 60 s.
  (12) The jobs and subscriptions are exported only through the worker-only entry. `index.ts` no longer exports `exportsJobs`, and the worker subscriptions test accepts `exportsWorker.register…` and checks the entry's jobs are pooled. A writer that drops a validated listing throws `PortalFeedError('WRITER_DROPPED')`: the job fails unrecoverably, and the ref is logged.
- 2026-10-23 · **Push portals, idealista and Fotocasa (S9-04):** (1) **Assumed API shape (H6):** both portals' partner documentation is not public. Assumed for both: OAuth2 client credentials (Basic `clientId:clientSecret` to a token URL, bearer afterwards), adverts keyed by our listing reference so `PUT {base}/{ref}` creates or replaces (idempotent: a lost answer cannot duplicate) and `DELETE` withdraws; JSON; whole euros; idealista `/v1/properties/{propertyCode}`, Fotocasa `/v2/ads/{externalId}`; the portal's own `id` in the answer, if any, is stored and used afterwards. Photo / description thresholds in the two profiles are guesses (`confirmed: false`). The exact pin is never sent (`showAddress: false`, `hideExactAddress: true`). (2) **Availability:** the catalog keeps both channels PLANNED; `exports.portal.<code>` on for an agency makes the channel AVAILABLE for it (list, create, change credentials) and lets the push job run; flag off: the connection is skipped as `writer-disabled` and nothing is sent or withdrawn. (3) **Sandbox vs production** is the base URL in the worker env, not a per-connection setting. Catalog credential fields stay `clientId`, `clientSecret` (an idealista customer code or similar may be needed: spec). (4) **A listing that fails the portal profile is not sent, and a synced advert stays** (taking an advert down for a missing photo seemed worse than a stale one; the reasons show as issues); withdrawal is only for listings the selection no longer returns (deselected, EXCLUDEd, not public, deleted). A withdrawn listing selected again is published again. (5) **Retry:** a retryable connection-level failure (429, 5xx, network) fails the job after the other connections have had their turn; the job retries 3 times with the 30 s exponential backoff; `Retry-After` is carried on the error but the backoff ignores it; permanent ones (auth rejected, credentials or endpoints missing, destination blocked) are reported in the job result and logs and not retried. A refused payload (other 4xx) is recorded FAILED with the code and not sent again until the content changes. (6) **No dashboard for push state yet:** per-listing state is in `portal_listing_sync`, the summary in the connection's `last_*` counts; connection-level stops are only in the job result / logs — a `/portals/[id]` push panel (state counts, FAILED listings with codes, last stop) is proposed as a follow-up. (7) **Mapping:** the base-locale text (the listing's own language when it has one), new-build units with the common fields only; no contact data is sent. (8) **Budgets:** calls are sequential; 200 calls and 8 minutes per connection and run, then the job queues itself 60 s later (already-synced listings cost no call, so each run advances). A push-only agency never gets a feed run, so the pass marks `nightly_at` for its push connections when the nightly pass queues the push. (9) **`safeFetch` writes:** POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE with a body (2 MiB), never following redirects; other callers are unchanged. (10) `portal_listing_sync`'s listing FK cascades: a purged listing's row (and its remote id) goes with it; listings are soft-deleted first, which the selection turns into a withdrawal.
- 2026-10-23 · **Push portals, review fixes (S9-04):** (1) **Teardown while the credentials exist:** a push connection is in SYNC mode (enabled, flag on, agency verified) or TEARDOWN mode (anything else): TEARDOWN withdraws every advert still up (rows with a remote id that are not WITHDRAWN and not a refused withdrawal), page by page, and costs no HTTP call when nothing is up. The feed pass hands every push-portal connection to the push job (enabled or not, token revoked or not: a revoked feed token means nothing to a push portal); the agency status subscriber queues a push run when the agency has a push connection. (2) **Deleting a connection:** *withdraw first*, not keep-the-rows: `deleteConnection` of a push connection that still has adverts up is refused (`VALIDATION_FAILED`, `reason: ADVERTS_LIVE`); the person switches the connection off, the push job takes the adverts down, then the delete is allowed (its sync rows cascade with it). A stop in between (`pushError`) shows why. (3) **Listing purge / agency deletion:** a listing is soft-deleted before any purge, which the selection turns into a withdrawal on the next run (the sync row's FK cascades only on the hard purge); a hard purge or an agency deletion that cascades the connection away *can* leave an advert at the portal - the purge paths do not call out to portals (no HTTP in a transaction); to be handled by the offboarding runbook (withdraw first). (4) **Exact coordinates** never leave: an EXACT pin is rounded to 3 decimals (about 110 m) for both portals until H6 confirms a portal-side hiding setting. (5) **No feed token for push portals:** a push connection still gets the generic token (the column is NOT NULL, the dashboard shows it), but no feed file is ever written for it, so its URL answers 404; hiding it in the UI is left to the `/portals/[id]` push panel follow-up. (6) **`portal_listing_sync` keeps the standard STRICT grants** (the registry has no read-only variant). (7) **Connections without a base URL** (`NOT_CONFIGURED` from missing env) are not stored on the connection (a deployment problem); the same code from a 3xx or a 404 on creating an advert (a wrong base URL) is. (8) **`Retry-After` is honoured only through the continuation job** (`max(Retry-After, 60 s)`, capped at 15 minutes by the client); a retryable failure without it still fails the job and retries with the 30 s exponential backoff.
